images.fact: Led India's peaceful struggle for independence from Britain (1869–1948).
French general who crowned himself Emperor and conquered much of Europe, until his defeat at Waterloo in 1815.
United the Mongol tribes and founded the largest land empire in history (c. 1162–1227).
US President who led the Union through the Civil War and ended slavery (1809–1865).
British Prime Minister who led the UK to victory in World War II.
The "Virgin Queen" of England. Her navy defeated the Spanish Armada in 1588.
Physicist behind the theory of relativity and E = mc² (1879–1955).
Roman general and dictator, famously stabbed in the Senate on the Ides of March, 44 BC.
Led the US civil rights movement and gave the "I Have a Dream" speech in 1963.
Jailed for 27 years for fighting apartheid, then became South Africa's first Black president.
Led America to victory in the War of Independence, then became the first US President.
Ruled Britain and its empire for 63 years (1837–1901). The Victorian era is named after her.
English king who had six wives and broke away from the Catholic Church (1491–1547).

images.description: Renaissance artist and inventor (red chalk drawing)
images.fact: Renaissance genius who painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, and sketched flying machines.

images.description: Physicist, laws of motion and gravity
images.fact: Discovered the laws of motion and gravity, supposedly after an apple fell (1643–1727).
Naturalist whose theory of evolution by natural selection changed science (1809–1882).
Discovered radium and polonium. The first person to win two Nobel Prizes.
Catholic nun who cared for the poorest people in Kolkata, India. Won the Nobel Peace Prize.
German philosopher who co-wrote The Communist Manifesto (1818–1883).
Led the 1917 Russian Revolution and founded the Soviet Union.
Ruled the Soviet Union as a dictator from the 1920s until 1953, including World War II.

images.description: Founder of the People's Republic of China
images.fact: Communist leader who founded the People's Republic of China in 1949.
Led the 1959 Cuban Revolution and ruled Cuba for nearly 50 years.
Argentine revolutionary in the Cuban Revolution. This photo is one of the most copied images ever.
Youngest elected US President. He was assassinated in Dallas in 1963.
The only US President elected four times. He led the US through the Great Depression and WWII.
US President and outdoorsman. The "teddy bear" is named after him.
Inventor of the practical light bulb, the phonograph and more than 1,000 other patents.
Inventor who pioneered AC electricity, which powers homes today (1856–1943).
US Founding Father who flew a kite in a thunderstorm to study electricity. He's on the $100 bill.
English playwright of Romeo and Juliet, Hamlet and Macbeth (1564–1616).
Child prodigy composer from Austria who wrote over 600 works (1756–1791).
German composer who kept writing music after going deaf, including the 9th Symphony.
Dutch painter of The Starry Night and Sunflowers. He sold almost no paintings in his life.
Spanish artist who co-founded Cubism and painted Guernica (1881–1973).
Mexican painter famous for bold, colourful self-portraits (1907–1954).
Italian astronomer who used a telescope to show the Earth goes around the Sun.
The "Sun King" of France, who built the Palace of Versailles and reigned for 72 years.
Queen of France, executed by guillotine in the French Revolution in 1793.
Russian tsar who modernised Russia and founded the city of St Petersburg.
Russia's longest-ruling female leader, who greatly expanded the empire (1729–1796).
Ancient Greek king who conquered an empire from Greece to India before turning 33.
Silent-film comedy star, famous as "The Tramp" with a bowler hat and cane.

images.description: Aviator, flew solo across the Atlantic
images.fact: The first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic. She vanished over the Pacific in 1937.
The first person to walk on the Moon, in 1969: "One small step for man..."

images.description: US civil rights activist, bus boycott
images.fact: Refused to give up her bus seat in 1955, sparking the Montgomery bus boycott.
Escaped slavery and became a famous writer and speaker against slavery in the US.
Escaped slavery and led many others to freedom on the Underground Railroad.
"The Lady with the Lamp", the founder of modern nursing, from the Crimean War.
Austrian doctor who founded psychoanalysis and studied dreams and the unconscious mind.

images.description: Queen of the UK and Australia, 1952–2022
images.fact: Britain's longest-reigning monarch, Queen for 70 years (1952–2022), including of Australia.
Led Vietnam's fight for independence. Saigon was renamed Ho Chi Minh City after him.
Founded the modern Republic of Turkey in 1923 and was its first president.
"The Liberator" who freed much of South America from Spain. Bolivia is named after him.
India's first Prime Minister after independence in 1947.
Britain's first female Prime Minister (1979–1990), nicknamed "the Iron Lady".
British explorer who mapped Australia's east coast in 1770.
Australian bushranger who fought police in homemade armour. He was hanged in 1880.
English novelist of Oliver Twist, A Christmas Carol and Great Expectations.
American writer of The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn.
Jewish girl whose diary of hiding from the Nazis in WWII became world famous.
Became deaf and blind as a baby, yet became an author and activist.
Italian artist who painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling and carved the statue of David.
Boy pharaoh of Egypt. His treasure-filled tomb was discovered in 1922.
German monk who started the Protestant Reformation in 1517.
Lakota leader who led his people at the Battle of the Little Bighorn in 1876.
Powerful US civil rights speaker and Black rights leader (1925–1965).
India's first and only female Prime Minister (no relation to Mahatma Gandhi).
Wrote the US Declaration of Independence and became the 3rd US President.

images.description: Last leader of the Soviet Union
images.fact: The last Soviet leader. He helped end the Cold War and won the Nobel Peace Prize.
Hollywood actor who became US President, famous for "Tear down this wall!"
Created Mickey Mouse and founded Disney and Disneyland.
Antarctic explorer who kept his whole crew alive after their ship Endurance sank in the ice.
American writer of dark tales and the poem The Raven (1809–1849).
Polish pope who led the Catholic Church for 26 years (1978–2005).
"The People's Princess", famous for her charity work. She died in a Paris car crash in 1997.
